naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This investment through USDA Rural Development will help the City of Chinook make upgrades and improvements to its wastewater infrastructure. This project will stabilize the riverbank nest to the wastewater treatment plant. Clay pipe will be replaced with larger diameter PVC sewer pipe improving the system reliability by replacing very old areas of the collection system and meeting minimum sewer pipe size requirements. The community's north lift station will be replaced entirely. Six troublesome manholes in frequently accessed areas will be replaced. Cracking and seepage in the digester wall will be corrected. Other site and building improvements will be completed and overall these system improvements will protect the local environment from contamination and safeguard public health.

naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to finance the infrastructure needed to deliver potable water to the city of Harlowton, which is a rural community approximately 130 miles east of Helena, Montana. The pipeline will also service about 40 rural towns that lie along the pipelines route and result in providing clean drinking water to Harlowtons residents as well as five other rural communities within central Montana. The proposed infrastructure consists of a disinfection building, pumps, a vault for a surge tank, a small building for housing controls, powerline installation, water tanks, a supervisory control and data acquisition system, a pressure reducing valve, an altitude valve, the connection to Harlowtons water tank, the various rural connections along the water pipeline, and approximately 24 miles of the water transmission main. The project is being funded through both a Water and Waste Disposable loan and a Water and Waste Disposable grant and will directly benefit over 1,000 Montana residents. These funds are leveraged against the Treasure State Regional Water Fund.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to pay for the costs to support Moon River Ranch LLC to rapidly scale its production of community-supported agriculture to support the food needs of its local community in Clinton, Montana. It will also fund the outreach and marketing needed to engage the local community as well as introduce other producers of eggs, meat, or other agricultural or food items into its distribution system. Moon River Ranch LLC will support its local communities of Clinton, Turah, Drummond, and other communities in Granite County, with fresh, locally grown produce. Much of this area is considered a "food desert," with extremely limited options for shopping. Bringing access to nutritious food to these communities is vital for the health of the communities and their residents. This local support also addresses a critical need that became apparent in 2020 through the COVID pandemic. Developing a reliable local source for a community food that is not reliant on traditional supply chains is necessary for food security. The goal of its project is to develop a naturally grown produce operation that will practice sustainable growing practices, utilizing season-extending tools like hoop-houses and greenhouses to extend the short Montana growing season. Montana agriculture will benefit in several ways. This project will allow the farm to provide nutritious produce to initially 50 families, to over 250 families in the next five years. It will also partner with other local ranches and farms to deliver their products to its members, and have them available for purchase online and at Farmers Markets.

Farmer Boy Eggs, LLC was established in 2016 by brothers Alex, Andrew, and Connor Verlanic and sells its eggs to 95 percent of the stores within a 60 mile radius of Drummond. These grant funds are critical for allowing Farmer Boy Eggs, LLC to buy larger orders of blank egg cartons and labels to have the inventory needed to maintain sales despite supply chain back-orders resulting from COVID-19. Farmer Boy Eggs, LLC is a staunch proponent of the local 4-H programs and purchases a handful of animals annually from the students to help grow student agriculture programs within this rural community.

naics_industry_sector: Public Administration
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to help Lake County Community Development Corporation (LCCDC), an economic development organization in Ronan, Montana, which is approximately 65 miles south of Kalispell. LCCDC identified the need to help businesses start up, grow and expand and will use this funding for business development, training and technical assistance in business planning, financial planning, market research, feasibility of products and services, cash flow management, strategic initiatives, and introductions to much-needed technology platforms to showcase and market small businesses. This funding will also support the inclusion of two entrepreneurs or small business owners to participate in Leadership Flathead Reservation (LFR) programming. Engaging new entrepreneurs in this program will open up new opportunities and encourage innovation by developing their leadership skills, increasing interactions within the business community, and building a stronger, more diverse economic base in Western Montana.

funding_code: RBCS ENTERPRISE GRANTS
naics_industry_sector: Public Administration
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will provide funding to Lake County Community Development Corporation (DBA) Mission West Community Development Partners (MWCDP), which is seeking an enterprise grant to conduct a feasibility study for a business accelerator and shared working space to be designated in downtown Polson, Montanas Tax Increment and Finance (TIF) district. Tis funding will be used to fully evaluate the concept of designating a regional co-working space and accelerator in Polson, which is approximately 50 miles south of Kalispell. The accelerator space will provide a shared space for entrepreneurs and prospective rural entrepreneurs to access trainings and receive information and resources specific to rural business. It will also support not only existing businesses but new and emerging businesses as well by providing them with access to resources and a collaborative space. With a low barrier to entry, community members of all backgrounds will have access to business supports that a standalone business might not otherwise access.

funding_code: RURAL COOPERATIVE DEVELOPMENT GRANTS
naics_industry_sector: Public Administration
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide a grant to Lake County Community Development Corporation. The mission of Lake County Community Development Corporation, doing business as Mission West Community Development Partners, is to enhance the quality of life and sustainable economic well-being of all residents of the rural communities it serves. As a cooperative development center since 1999, cooperative development has been a key tool used by Mission West as a community and economic development strategy in rural Western Montana. Mission West recognizes the potential for cooperatives to help rural communities in Western Montana build robust and sustainable economies, increase community wealth, access critical services, support the work force, and improve quality of life. This project seeks to improve the economic condition and assist in COVID-19 recovery of rural areas through cooperative development, including the operation of a cooperative development center; effective delivery of cooperative development services to rural areas of Western Montana; expanding and strengthening the cooperative development ecosystem; technical assistance to new, emerging cooperatives and new services to further development of existing cooperatives; outreach and education related to cooperatives; program monitoring and evaluation; and strong partnerships that advance cooperative economic development and introduce new models.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to help REcreate Designs LLC, an adult and childrens clothing line, accessories, and home goods made from upcycled materials, make energy-efficiency improvements to their operations. REcreate Designs has been in business since 2005 and is located in St. Ignatius, Montana, about 40 miles north of Missoula. They employ local people and source raw materials from thrift and second-hand outlets and repurpose them into their products. REcreate Designs keeps an estimated 3,000 pounds of waste out of the landfills every year and is proud to be 100 percent made in Montana. Project funds will be used to make energy efficiency improvements with the purchase a new front door and energy-efficient lighting. These upgrades will save the business about $2,100 per year and reduce energy consumption by 7,325 kilowatt hours (kWh) or by nearly 31 percent. This is enough electricity to power one home annually.

Funds will be used to provide technical assistance and training to rural micro-entrepreneurs and microenterprises in Lake County. Lake County Community Development Corporation has previously received two Rural Development Rural Microentrepreneur Assistance Program revolving loans and 10 grants since 2010. funding_code: LAMP BEGINNING AND SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED FARMERS OR RANCHERS GRANTS - COVID
naics_industry_sector: Manufacturing
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to fund a feasibility study and business plan to assess the viability of a mobile processing unit and cut-and-wrap enterprise for Tribally-produced beef and bison on the Flathead Indian reservation located in Montana. The Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes is a Federally recognized tribe that will contract with a consultant to conduct a market analysis and study to test the feasibility of developing a dual bison and beef meat processing enterprise. The goal of the mobile processing enterprise is to increase local food security and create economic opportunity for the tribe and its members. The importance of food security has become even more apparent during the COVID-19 pandemic when out-of-state meat processing plants were forced to close, and the meat supply was threatened. The proposed business would be a mobile slaughter unit designed to slaughter and partially process grass-fed bison naturally, in their own environment on the National Bison Range, without added stress. The mobile slaughter unit would also provide services to Tribal member cattle producers to slaughter and partially process cattle on-ranch. The revenue derived from the bison production will be utilized to further support conservation of the National Bison Range.

naics_industry_sector: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Hunting
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to pay for the costs of processing dried herbal tea and culinary herbs for Awesome Acres LLC, a small farm located in St. Ignatius, Montana. The farm has been in operation for the last six years and is focused on growing and drying herbs. This project focuses on utilizing the farm-grown raw herbs that, when fresh, can only be sold locally for two months out of the year, and turn them into shelf-stable dried teas and culinary herbs that can be sold throughout the entire year. This year, Awesome Acres, LLC is substantially increasing its herb growing and drying capacity with a new greenhouse and a larger drying shed. The funding from this project will enable it to process their herbs more efficiently, expand into new markets and increase its customer base and the planned income from this project will enable Awesome Acres, LLC to hire a seasonal farm worker, upgrade garden tools, and purchase multiple tractor implements.

naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used for upgrading the Wastewater Treatment Plant for the City of Hardin. The City of Hardin wastewater system consists of a gravity sewer system with a lift station and an oxidation ditch mechanical treatment system that was built in 1978. Treated effluent is discharged to the Bighorn River. Improvements planned for the Hardin Wastewater System include installation of new sewer main and manholes identified in a recent Infiltration and Inflow Study as in need of replacement. The mechanical plant will be upgraded by replacing the headworks structure and adding a new Intermittent Cycle Extended Aeration System continuous flow SBR, converting the existing oxidation ditch to surge flow equalization, and correcting individual issues within the system. Other upgrades will include a new plant water well, septage receiving station, installation of a backup power generator, a new redundant UV disinfection system, and an administration building for lab space and the UV system. This project will be conducted into three phases.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to cover a cost-overrun resulting from the recent bid opening. The project scope remains the same, which is to replace and upsize cast iron water mains within the system with minimum 8-inch diameter PVC water mains. The existing water system was originally constructed in 1919. Much of the original cast iron main installed is still in service. This pipe has badly deteriorated over time, and City personnel repair an average of 5-8 leaks each year. Corrosion in the mains has led to high levels of iron, manganese, sulphur, and total dissolved solids (TDS) in the water. There are potential health risks due to these elements in the water. The City system loses an average of over 40% of their pumped water annually. The fragile mains are known to fracture during fire events. 16 fire hydrants are inoperable and another 32 hydrants need to be added to the system to meet DEQ Circular 1 and NFPA fire code regulations. An 8-block area in the middle of the City does not currently have coverage from hydrants.

funding_code: RBCS ENTERPRISE GRANTS
naics_industry_sector: Public Administration
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to fund targeted technical assistance, training, and other activities provided by Lake County Community Development Corporation (LCCDC) leading to the development and/or expansion of small and emerging, private business in rural Lake, Mineral and Sanders counties. The focus of the assistance will be LCCDC hosting 40 business development workshops within the region over the next 12 months. LCCDC also plans to provide client technical assistance by LCCDC staff and its expert network of professional service providers. It is estimated that 200 hours of direct expert assistance will be provided to individual businesses. Additionally, LCCDC staff worked with an advisory board to develop Leadership Flathead Reservation, a program that builds entrepreneurial skills and creates a network of business leaders throughout the Flathead Reservation. LCCDC is funding a total of four entrepreneurs to participate in the program. The participants will use the skills learned to make positive contributions to the Reservations small business community. The benefit of this workshop will be in bridging cultural divides to enable non-tribal businesses to work with tribal individuals, companies, and organizations. Lastly, a pilot program will use the Value Builder System, an online tool that assesses a businesss current valuation, identifies areas of improvement, prioritizes the highest impact areas to build on, and identifies red flags that could be impediments to a successful transition for succession planning. In partnership with the Small Business Development Center in Kalispell and Flathead Valley Community College, LCCDC staff will work with clients through the Value Builder System to build and document value in the business and develop a plan for business succession.

funding_code: RURAL COOPERATIVE DEVELOPMENT GRANTS
naics_industry_sector: Public Administration
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide technical assistance for rural cooperative development. Lake County Community Development Corporation (LCCDC) established a cooperative development program in 1999 under funding from USDA-Rural Developments RCDG program. The cooperative development program is an integral part of LCCDCs overall purpose and economic development strategy of providing technical assistance and access to capital resources to new and expanding businesses throughout the rural region and the Flathead Indian Reservation in northwest Montana. LCCDC provides expertise in cooperative development through trainings, technical assistance, partnerships and assessment to individuals and entities in the startup, expansion, or operational improvement of their cooperative businesses. LCCDC has capacity to deliver technical assistance through one-on-one sessions; workshops and trainings; educational materials, resources and publications; and contracts for specialized expertise. The potential to deliver effective technical assistance has been demonstrated by the outcomes: the successful launch and incorporation of cooperatives and mutually owned businesses and job creation within rural communities. In the past five years, there have been 12 businesses incorporated with assistance from LCCDC. LCCDC helped to create 30 jobs and save 100 jobs as a result of this assistance.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will study and explore the market demand for culled cows that are raised and processed in a conservation-friendly manner. The Blackfoot Valley includes the lands that surround the tributaries to the Blackfoot River in western Montana. The focus area is directly east of Missoula, Montana, and extends further east across Twin Creeks, Potomac, Ovando, and Helmville, Montana. Producers in the Blackfoot Valley have a strong reputation for conservation leadership throughout Montana, the West, and the nation. This study will look into whether that reputation can be marketed to bring an added value to the producer and build more stability for local producer business models. Funds will be used to conduct a market assessment of regional meat products. The primary goal of this study is to uncover the added consumer value as well as the estimated price point for conservation-friendly meat. The study will deliver a price per lbs. estimate as well as a head per week and head/month demand figure for the culled cow market in Lewis & Clark, Missoula, and Powell counties. Mannix Brothers Ranch and others will use this information to determine whether there is sufficient demand for Mannix and their neighbors to increase culled cow production. It will also guide their decision to individually or collectively brand their products and inform the producers on whether a feasibility project on new production and delivery methods, including direct to consumer meat products, should be pursued.

Roxann (owner) has produced wines there from grapes sourced around Montana and Washington resulting in several gold medals, and wines for sale locally since October 2018. Of the 22 acres available for vines, 25% have been planted providing the first harvest last fall of 2019. 2020 projections of a 10-ton harvest will provide 550 cases of wine. Willow Mountain Winerys workplan and budget will support the growth of the business as well as the wine industry in the state of Montana. naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to connect additional users to the Thompson Falls wastewater treatment and collection system, and to make significant improvements to the existing wastewater treatment system. The City of Thompson Falls currently serves approximately one-quarter of the city residents and businesses. The portion of the community that is not served treats their wastewater with sub-standard septic systems. The homes are located on lots that are too small to install approved, modern septic treatment systems. This contributes to degraded groundwater quality in the community. This phase of the project will connect approximately 126 residential users and 4 other users. This is in addition to the 190 users added in the previously approved funding. This funding will also provide for construction of improvements to the existing wastewater treatment plant. Additional treatment processes will be added as well as disinfection of the effluent produced by the system. The treatment plant improvements will allow the city to stay in compliance with their wastewater discharge permit. This will result in modern, reliable wastewater treatment and improved groundwater quality which will improve the overall environment of the community as well as improved water quality in the Clark Fork River. Improved infrastructure will facilitate the economic development efforts of the community. This project is phase one and two of a four phase project to provide sewer service to the entire community of Thompson Falls. By funding phases one and two simultaneously, there will be economies of scale in both the engineering and construction costs of the project.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development loan guarantee investment will be used to provide Montana Craft Malt Company (MCM) working capital using the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act (CARES Act). In February 2020, MCM became fully operational to malt barley for beer brewers/distillers. MCM had signed contracts with brewers and distillers, however, these partners were forced to back out of these agreements due to the state of Montanas government ordering a state-wide lockdown to protect citizens from COVID 19. MCM experienced decreased demand due to taproom and restaurant closures. Also, MCMs distributors stopped accepting its product because of the pandemic. Overall, COVID-19 has reduced the market for MCMs malt product. MCM is the first commercial malt manufacturer of its kind and produces specialty malt for craft breweries in Montana and beyond. MCM employs 11 individuals located in rural areas (Butte, Montana located in Butte-Silverbow County) and provides economic sustainability in the rural community. After weathering COVID 19, MCM expects to be a strong business which will partner solely with rural Montana farmers for grain to malt. This grain from Montana is "Made in America" and the sale of it will support and strengthen not only the agricultural producer but the rural economy the farmer lives in; leading to the viability of their rural community. MCM also plans to export 25% of its products to markets abroad and boost our countrys global competitiveness.

naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to conduct an Infiltration and Inflow Study for the wastewater system for the City of Hardin, which has 3,505 users. The city of Hardin is faced with deficiencies throughout its aging wastewater treatment facility. The current wastewater treatment system was built in 1978 and has not been updated significantly since construction. Most of the sub-systems within the existing wastewater treatment facility do not meet Montana Department of Environmental Quality design standards or Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) regulations. The EPA conducted a compliance evaluation inspection in September of 2017 and the findings of this inspection resulted in a "Significant Noncompliance" status for the wastewater treatment facility. Without upgrades to the wastewater treatment system, residents will face a series of permit violations, possible enforcement actions, and, in the event a connection moratorium is issued, lost economic opportunities, which would adversely affect the community. Additional funding includes $15,000 from the State of Montana and a $3,200 applicant contribution.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to assist, Alan Albert Boomer to purchase and install a 13,400 kWh solar system to power a cattle ranch running 180 black angus cows. The system will help power the garage where Boomer uses tools to make, repair and maintain farm machinery, haying equipment and cattle panels. This affects all aspects of which make the ranch operate on a day-to-day basis; from salting, livestock checks, fencing, feeding, and animal round-ups. The garage also houses the tractors to use to feed and care for livestock which are plugged-in during cold weather months. The solar array will also offset costs to power the lights for nighttime calving and lambing and to run calf warmers and heat lamps. The power will also run the water pump to 3 geo-thermal water tanks, power the cattle scales during the time to ship the calves out and run the branding irons and dehorners when working cattle during spring branding. The ranch uses power for almost everything related to cattle ranching and would not be able to continue this lifestyle if reliable and affordable power was not available. This project replaces 13,400 kWh of electricity per year which is enough electricity to power one home and saves the farm $1,514 in annual energy costs. The purpose of this funding program is to assist farmers, ranchers, and rural small businesses in developing renewable energy systems, and in making energy-efficiency improvements to their operations. $15,132 Owner Funds $20,176 Total Project Costs

funding_code: RURAL COOPERATIVE DEVELOPMENT GRANTS
naics_industry_sector: Public Administration
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide technical assistance for rural cooperative development. Lake County Community Development Corporation (LCCDC) established a cooperative development program in 1999 under funding from USDA-Rural Developments RCDG program. The cooperative development program is an integral part of LCCDCs overall purpose and economic development strategy of providing technical assistance and access to capital resources to new and expanding businesses throughout the rural region and the Flathead Indian Reservation in northwest Montana. project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to assist in improving an essential community service to a local, rural community. The Troy Rural Fire District located in northwest Montana was seeking a way to obtain funding to convert two military surplus 6 X 6 chassis trucks into water tankers for firefighting and suppression purposes. Troy Rural Fire Districts two primary service areas are located in heavily forested areas and covered with two satellite stations with separate coverage areas. In addition to these coverage areas, the District provides coverage through mutual aid agreements. Each water tanker will provide 3,000 gallons of water to be available per station to respond to fire and suppression calls until other firefighters arrive on scene. The estimated in-service date for the converted vehicles will be the spring of 2019, and during the off season will be located in heated facilities and able to assist other local fire departments. Equipment for each converted tanker truck will consist of the tank, painting, radios and lighting. The converted equipment will improve the firefighters response ability to improve public safety and overall effectiveness of the Troy Rural Fire District. This equipment will greatly enhance their ability to effectively respond and provide emergency services in the rural areas of northwest Montana and to the outlying areas of the city of Troy, Montana. This investment will benefit the 938 residents in Troy and the 1135 residents in outlying areas.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development loan guarantee investment will be used to term out interim/construction financing used to facilitate the construction of a new malting plant for Montana Craft Malt Company (MCM), a start-up business. It will be the first commercial malt manufacturer of its kind and will produce specialty malt for craft breweries in Montana and beyond. MCM will offer 15 jobs to employ capable individuals located in rural areas (Butte, Montana located in Butte-Silverbow County) and will provide economic sustainability in the rural community. MCM expects to be a strong business which will partner solely with rural Montana farmers for grain to malt. This grain from Montana is "Made in America" and the sale of it will support and strengthen not only the agricultural producer but the rural economy the farmer lives in; leading to the viability of their rural community. MCM also plans to export 25% of its products to markets abroad and boost our countrys global competitiveness. MCM is utilizing nearly 50% of its own private capital to fund this project; leveraging resources to support America. $11,500,000 - Borrower Contribution $ 3,500,000 - TrailWest Bank Loan $25,000,000 - Total Project Cost
